title: What Kind of Lover Are You?

chapters.title: How you fall
chapters.teaser: Fast, slow, sideways or all at once. The way your soul actually falls for someone.

chapters.title: Your flirting style
chapters.teaser: What you think you're doing, what they think you're doing, and the one move that lands.

chapters.title: Your attachment pattern
chapters.teaser: Clingy, cool, steady or somewhere in between. How you hold on when you care.

chapters.title: Jealousy and your trigger
chapters.teaser: The exact thing that sets you off, and what you do instead of saying it.

chapters.title: Yeon's red flag report
chapters.teaser: The love habit you keep repeating. Yeon does not soften this chapter.

chapters.title: What you actually need
chapters.teaser: Not your type. Your match. The kind of person and love that lets you relax.

text.how-you-fall: You fall for the details. Sin is the jewel, the polished silver ring, metal that has already been refined into something beautiful. You notice how someone dresses, how they speak to waiters, whether they text in full sentences. Taste matters to you more than you'd admit. When someone passes your many quiet tests, you fall gracefully and with real tenderness. You make love feel elegant and special, like being invited into a beautiful room. Underneath the polish, though, you're sensitive. A careless comment can stay with you for weeks, and you might pull back before you're hurt, just in case. You also fall for an idea of perfection sometimes, and real people, with their messy kitchens and odd habits, can never quite match it. Let them be imperfect. So are you.
text.flirting: The way you flirt is refined and slightly mysterious. A well-timed compliment, a glance, a perfectly chosen gift that shows you noticed exactly what they like. You're elegant without trying, and people often feel slightly nervous around you because you seem so put together. You also flirt through banter: witty, a little cutting, always clever. The issue is that you can be so polished that people can't tell if you like them or if this is simply your default charm. And you hate rejection so much that you rarely risk being clear. Try letting one crack show. A slightly embarrassing story, a real laugh, a direct "I've been hoping you'd text." The jewel shines brighter when it catches light, and light gets in through the cracks.
text.attachment: Your pattern leans anxious under a cool surface. You present calm and composed, but inside you're constantly reading for signs of rejection or disapproval. Criticism stings you deeply, even gentle, well-meant criticism, and you might replay a small comment for days. Because you hate being seen as needy, you rarely ask for reassurance. Instead you withdraw, go a little icy, and wait for the other person to come and find you. If they don't, you take it as confirmation. When you feel secure, you're devoted, thoughtful and wonderfully romantic, with an eye for beauty that makes everyday moments feel special. The work is telling your partner when something hurt, gently and quickly, before it hardens into distance.
text.jealousy: Jealousy, for you, is about comparison. You notice the person who seems more beautiful, more successful, more effortlessly cool, and you quietly measure yourself against them. You won't admit it, of course. You'd rather die than appear insecure. So you go cool and slightly sarcastic, and your partner feels a chill without understanding why. Your trigger is being outshone or taken for granted. You put a lot of care into how you love, and you need it noticed. The healthier version is honesty with a light touch. "I felt a bit invisible tonight" is small, true and much more effective than a frosty silence. People who love you want to reassure you. Give them the chance, instead of making them guess why the temperature dropped.
text.red-flag: The short version, from Yeon: you're a perfectionist in love, and nobody passes inspection. You notice their posture in photos, their grammar in texts, the way they chew, and you file every flaw away until the list is longer than the reasons you liked them. Second flag: you punish with coldness. When hurt, you go elegant and icy, perfectly polite and completely unreachable, which is somehow worse than shouting. Third: your pride can make you leave first just so you don't get left. You'd rather end something beautiful than risk being disappointed by it. You deserve a love that feels precious. Precious doesn't mean flawless. Sometimes the best jewelry has a little wear on it from being loved.
text.what-you-need: You need gentleness and appreciation. A partner who notices the effort you put into everything and says so, who gives feedback kindly and never mocks your sensitivity. You need someone with taste, or at least curiosity, who enjoys the beautiful things you love: the good café, the thoughtful gift, the evening that feels curated. You also need a lot of reassurance delivered without drama, and someone who stays warm when you go cool. And you need space to be private. You open slowly, and pressure makes you close faster. The best person for you treats you like something precious without putting you on a shelf. Admired, protected, and still allowed to be human.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Sin, you love like a jewel. Elegant, thoughtful, everything you touch feels special.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: And you judged their font choice in the group chat. Don't lie.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: You have beautiful taste! People feel honored to be chosen by you.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: When you're hurt, you go so polite it's terrifying. Ice queen behavior.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: Tell them gently when something stings. They want to make it right.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Nobody passes inspection. Stop inspecting. Start enjoying.

spring.intro: Born while Wood rules, and with Metal controlling Wood, a spring-born Sin Metal is a jewel set in a garden, beautiful and constantly evaluating the blossoms around it. You have high standards in love and you are not shy about them. You notice the outfit, the grammar, the way someone treats the waiter. The season keeps you busy pursuing and choosing, which can make dating feel like curating. Many promising people are dismissed for a small flaw. Earth, your resource, gives you security, and with security comes generosity. When you trust that you are valued, you relax your rules and let someone be imperfect and lovely at the same time.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Spring Sin, you ghosted them over their font choice. Yes, I saw. Give imperfection one more date.

summer.intro: Summer puts Fire in command, and Fire controls Metal. A jewel left in the summer heat feels the pressure most, so a summer-born Sin Metal is sensitive, precise and quick to feel judged. In love you crave admiration but flinch from criticism, and intense, demanding partners can leave you feeling scratched. You often test people to see whether they will still treat you gently when you are difficult. The heat also gives you depth and resilience you rarely credit yourself with. Earth softens Fire and protects the gem, so look for steady, patient love rather than dramatic passion. You sparkle brightest in shade, with someone who handles you with care.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Summer Sin, you're precious, not fragile. Choose someone gentle enough to know the difference.

autumn.intro: In autumn Metal takes the lead, so an autumn-born Sin is a jewel in its element, polished and certain of its worth. In love you are discerning, elegant and quietly proud. You know exactly the kind of devotion you deserve, and you are not afraid to walk away from anything less. With doubled Metal, the blind spot is perfectionism and coolness. You can withhold affection to make a point, or expect a partner to read your standards without being told. Water, your output element, washes a jewel until it gleams. In love that is open expression: telling them what pleases you, what hurts, what you want next. Mystery attracts. Clarity keeps.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Autumn Sin, your silent treatment is beautifully executed. It's still a silent treatment. Use words.

winter.intro: Water rules winter, and Metal produces Water. Classical saju says Sin Metal loves to be washed by clear water, so a winter-born Sin is a gem in a cold stream: luminous, articulate and a little chilled. You express feelings with precision. Your texts are thoughtful and your compliments land. But giving so much through words can leave you emotionally thin, and the cold season makes you private about needing comfort. You may pull back exactly when you most want closeness. Earth, your resource, means security, and Fire brings warmth. A partner who offers both, a steady presence and an obvious delight in you, lets you sparkle without shivering.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Winter Sin, you write the loveliest messages. Let someone warm you up in return.

earth.intro: Earth-days Sin, you're a jewel in rich ground. Earth feeds Metal, but heavy soil can hide a gem, and you sometimes hide your wants to keep things pleasant. In love you're refined, thoughtful and noticeably selective. You show care through details. The risk is waiting for your person to read standards you've never said. You need a partner who appreciates precision and asks what matters to you. Then you need to answer, honestly, the first time they ask.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Sin, they can't meet a standard you've kept secret.

strength.strong: A strong Sin Metal is a jewel that knows its exact carat. With plenty of Metal and Earth in your chart, you are elegant, discerning and very clear about what you deserve. In love that can turn into exacting standards and quiet judgment. Your blind spot is overpowering with perfectionism: correcting small things, withholding warmth when disappointed, expecting a partner to anticipate your wishes. Pride protects you, and it can also keep people at arm's length. Practice praising out loud more often than you critique. Let imperfect gestures count. The finest jewel still needs a setting that holds it.
strength.weak: A weak Sin Metal is a delicate gem without a protective setting. With little Metal or Earth support, you are sensitive to criticism and quick to doubt your worth in love. You may accept less than you want, then feel hurt that nobody noticed your standards. Your blind spot is shrinking: dulling your opinions, accepting careless treatment, telling yourself you are too demanding. You are not. Say what you like, gently and specifically. People who value you will be glad to know. The ones who dismiss it were never handling you with care anyway.

balance_text.too_much_wood: Too much Wood in your chart turns love into a growth plan. You want things to move forward, define the relationship, make progress, and slow phases make you restless. You can also be stubborn in arguments, holding your position like a tree in wind. In love this looks like big intentions and a little impatience. Balance it with Metal energy: clear agreements, pruning what isn't working, and accepting that some things are already finished growing. Not every relationship needs to become a forest. Some are perfect as a single, steady tree.
balance_text.missing_wood: Missing Wood means beginnings are your hard part. You might hold back until someone else makes the first move, define things, or suggest the next step, and you can stay in a comfortable but stuck situation for too long. Your love is real, it just doesn't push. Balance it by practicing small starts: suggest the date, send the first text, say what you hope for out loud. Green things help as reminders, a plant by your bed, a green phone case. Love grows when someone plants it. Sometimes that someone is you.
balance_text.too_much_fire: Too much Fire makes your love bright, fast and a little combustible. You fall hard and feel everything at full volume, whether you show it out loud or keep it behind your eyes. The highs are glorious. The lows, when attention drops, feel like the lights went out. You can also lose interest once the excitement settles. Balance it with Water energy: slowing down, letting quiet evenings count, and sitting with feelings before reacting. Ask yourself if you love the person or the thrill. The best flame for you burns steady, not just bright.
balance_text.missing_fire: Missing Fire means passion and visibility don't come easily in love. You might care deeply but struggle to show it, hold back affection until you're sure, or feel awkward with romantic gestures. People can mistake your reserve for disinterest. Balance it by letting warmth out in small, brave doses: a compliment, a hug that lasts a second longer, a little playfulness. Warm colors and sunlight help you feel more expressive. You don't need fireworks. You just need people to see that the light is on.
balance_text.too_much_earth: Too much Earth makes you a steady, devoted partner who can get a little stuck. You value security, routine and loyalty, and you might stay in familiar patterns even when they've stopped making you happy. Change feels risky. You may also over-care, taking on your partner's problems as your own. Balance it with Wood energy: try something new together, plan an adventure, let the relationship grow in surprising directions. Safe is wonderful. Safe and alive is even better.
balance_text.missing_earth: Missing Earth means love can feel unsteady. You might worry about where things stand, struggle to settle into commitment, or jump between highs and lows. You can also find it hard to trust that someone will stay. Balance it by building small, reliable rituals: a weekly date, a regular call, a shared routine. Choose partners who are consistent rather than exciting. Earth tones and home-cooked meals help you feel grounded. Stability isn't boring. For you, it's what lets love feel safe enough to enjoy.
balance_text.too_much_metal: Too much Metal gives you strong standards and very clear boundaries in love. You know what you want and what you won't tolerate, which is healthy, until it becomes rigid. You can be critical, quick to judge, or end things abruptly when disappointed. Balance it with Fire energy: warmth, forgiveness, play. Let small mistakes be small. Say the kind thing before the honest thing. Strong boundaries keep you safe. Soft edges let people actually come close enough to love you.
balance_text.missing_metal: Missing Metal means boundaries are your hard part in love. You might say yes when you mean no, stay too long, or let people treat you less well than you deserve because you don't want conflict. Your heart is open, sometimes too open. Balance it by practicing clear, simple limits: "I'm not okay with that," without a long explanation. Decluttering and white or silver accents can help you feel sharper. Boundaries aren't walls. They're the frame that makes the picture of your love clear.
balance_text.too_much_water: Too much Water makes your love deep, intuitive and sometimes overwhelming. You feel everything, read every mood and can get lost in emotional currents or imagined stories. You may also avoid commitment, drifting rather than choosing. Balance it with Earth energy: grounding conversations, practical plans, partners who are steady and clear. Write down what actually happened before reacting to what you feel happened. Your depth is beautiful. It just needs a shore so you don't get swept away.
balance_text.missing_water: Missing Water means emotional depth and rest don't come easily in love. You might stay busy, keep conversations practical, or struggle to sit with vulnerable feelings, yours or your partner's. Love can feel like a to-do list. Balance it with slow, quiet moments: late talks, journaling, listening without fixing. Navy and black, water by your bed, and slow evenings help you soften. You don't need to drown in feelings. Just let yourself wade in a little deeper.

too_much_wood.speaker: yeon
too_much_wood.text: Too much Wood: you want it defined, labeled and growing by Thursday. Breathe.

too_much_wood.speaker: bom
too_much_wood.text: Your hope is beautiful. Let it grow at the speed of a real person.

too_much_fire.speaker: yeon
too_much_fire.text: Too much Fire: you fall hard and fast, out loud or in silence. Then the second act bores you.

too_much_fire.speaker: bom
too_much_fire.text: Your passion is a gift. Let it simmer a while. Slow love tastes better.

too_much_earth.speaker: yeon
too_much_earth.text: Too much Earth: staying somewhere stale because leaving takes effort isn't loyalty. It's inertia.

too_much_earth.speaker: bom
too_much_earth.text: Your loyalty is rare. Make sure it's going somewhere that still feeds you.

too_much_metal.speaker: yeon
too_much_metal.text: Too much Metal: your dating checklist has forty points. Nobody passes. Including you.

too_much_metal.speaker: bom
too_much_metal.text: Standards protect you. Leave one door open for someone surprising.

too_much_water.speaker: yeon
too_much_water.text: Too much Water: you wrote a whole love story in your head. They've read none of it.

too_much_water.speaker: bom
too_much_water.text: Your depth is gorgeous. Share a little of it with the real person.

missing_wood.speaker: bom
missing_wood.text: Missing Wood? Love won't start itself. Send the first text. Plant something.

missing_wood.speaker: yeon
missing_wood.text: Waiting for them to make the move isn't patience. It's hiding behind a nice word.

missing_fire.speaker: bom
missing_fire.text: Missing Fire? Your love is real, it just whispers. Let someone hear it.

missing_fire.speaker: yeon
missing_fire.text: A compliment you only think doesn't count. Say it, then survive the blushing.

missing_earth.speaker: bom
missing_earth.text: Missing Earth? You love brightly but drift. A small weekly ritual keeps you anchored.

missing_earth.speaker: yeon
missing_earth.text: Three crushes, zero follow-through. Pick one and show up twice in a row.

missing_metal.speaker: bom
missing_metal.text: Missing Metal? Your kindness needs a boundary. A no keeps your yes worth something.

missing_metal.speaker: yeon
missing_metal.text: Three cancellations and a fourth chance isn't generosity. It's a pattern you're funding.

missing_water.speaker: bom
missing_water.text: Missing Water? You act before you feel. Pause and ask what you actually want.

missing_water.speaker: yeon
missing_water.text: Over someone in a weekend isn't healing. It's skipping the chapter. Read it.
